title: EU Data Scoping & Customer Gating: decision flow and fallback model matrix
creator: Maya Thompson
description: We need an auditable enforcement layer that scopes customer traffic to EU-only compute when their tenancy or contract requires data residency. This ticket captures the decision flow for customer allowlists/denylists, the tier-routing behavior when reserved capacity is unavailable, and the canonical fallback matrix of model variants (same-accuracy EU-hosted variant, reduced-capacity EU fallback, global model with redaction) to minimize customer impact while preserving compliance. The goal is to produce an implementable spec and a set of unit/integration tests so the policy engine can run deterministically at the edge router and at the control plane policy evaluation service.
acceptance_criteria: Policy decision graph covering: customer residency flag, contract clauses, explicit allow/deny lists, and emergency override
Routing behavior defined for 5 scenarios (normal capacity, dedicated saturated, region outage, cross-border cache hit, onboarding with unclear residency)
Fallback model matrix specifying variant mapping, quality degradation expectation, and SLOs for each fallback
Audit log schema and sample events for every state transition (decision_reason, policy_version, matched_rules)
Automated test harness (policy unit tests + e2e smoke tests) wired into CI with sample tenants
Confluence spec + RFC linked and reviewed by Security & Legal
Feature gated behind runtime flag and staged rollout plan for 2 customers in Canary
implementation_plan: Draft policy DSL extensions (edge-matchers for country-residency, contract-tag-based allowlist/denylist, explicit customer_gate boolean)
Add a deterministic tie-break order: 1) explicit deny, 2) explicit allow, 3) contract residency true, 4) inferred residency from billing region
Update policy decision service to return (route_region, model_variant, decision_reason, policy_version)
Router integration to obey route_region and reject non-EU egress when route_region == EU_ONLY unless override is present
Define fallback matrix and implement model variant selector in runtime (variant IDs + quantization profiles)
Extend audit log schema and wire to console + compliance retention store
Create canary config: 2 tenants (one POC EU enterprise, one test tenant) with runtime flag off-by-default
Write unit tests for cases: allowlist match, denylist match, contract-residency, capacity-fallback, outage-fallback
decisions: Use explicit deny precedence over allow to avoid accidental compliance breaches (legal review agreed)
Do not rely solely on IP geolocation for residency — billing tag + contract metadata are primary sources

Fallback preference order: EU-hosted identical model variant -> EU small-quantized variant -> EU degraded throughput pool -> block request with guidance -> global model only with data-redaction if customer opted-in
Cache scoping: KV cache entries that contain PII or sensitive prefixes must be tagged with region scope and never replicated outside EU scope
Make policy_version explicit in every routing decision event to allow post-hoc audits and rollbacks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reserved EU capacity exhausted -> mitigation: autoscale reserved pool and configure chaos alerts to SRE; prioritized traffic for P1 customers
Risk: Incorrect allowlist entry causes service to route out-of-region -> mitigation: two-step verification for allowlist changes (owner + sec approval) and preview simulation mode
Risk: Latency/regression when enforcing policy at edge -> mitigation: precompile decision rules into efficient evaluation tree and benchmark under load
Risk: KV cache leakage across regions -> mitigation: add region-scope tagging at write path and GC policy to scrub replicated entries
